questions.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find $a+b+c,$ given that the matrix form of the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ a & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $T$ gives us the following information:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-9 & 2 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{-1\cdot (-9)-2\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -4 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-4+(-9)+20=7.
$$

questions.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation $T$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find $a+b+c,$ given that the matrix form of the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a & 5 \\ b & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}c \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix form of $T$ gives us the following information:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot (-2)-5\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-3+(-1)+8=4.
$$

questions.problem:
The affine transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2u-3v+2,\,y=6v-3u-4.
$$

Given that the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ of $T$ is

$$
u=2x+y+a,\,v=x+by+c,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Reversing the action of $T,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Au+b & =x \\ Au & =x-b \\ u & ={A}^{-1}(x-b).\end{aligned}
$$

So, writing our transformation in matrix form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-3v+2 \\ 6v-3u-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-3v \\ -3u+6v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the inverse of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u} & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{A}^{-1}}\cdot ({{[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}-{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x-2 \\ y+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\cdot (x-2)+1\cdot (y+4) \\ 1\cdot (x-2)+(\frac{2}{3})\cdot (y+4)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x+y \\ x+\frac{2}{3}y+\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, the inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}$ in coordinate form is

$$
u=2x+y+0,\,v=x+\frac{2}{3}y+\frac{2}{3}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=0+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3}.
$$
